steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper evaluating ChatGPT on dialogue discourse analysis, i.e., topic segmentation and discourse parsing. It should motivate the study, describe how we prompted and evaluated it, and summarize the main findings.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Motivation: LLMs like ChatGPT are strong on NLG/NLU, but no evaluation yet on dialogue discourse analysis
- What dialogue discourse analysis is: topic segmentation and discourse parsing; why it is a hard test
- Our method: prompt design and experimental setup
- Main findings on topic and rhetorical structures
- Further studies: in-context learning, prompt ablation, instruction following
- Closing hope

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Motivation
  - generative models -> LLMs (e.g. ChatGPT) remarkable on NLG and NLU tasks
  - but: no qualitative/quantitative evaluation of ChatGPT on dialogue discourse analysis
  - evaluation needed to uncover potential for deep semantic understanding of conversations
- Dialogue discourse analysis
  - crucial in NLP; reveals underlying topic, coherence, rhetorical structures in dialogue
  - previous work: dialogue topic segmentation (linear topic structures) and discourse parsing (hierarchical rhetorical structures); Figure 1
  - ChatGPT = most recent language generation capability; its discourse structure understanding largely uncharted
  - unlike tasks needing only shallow understanding (extract output from input), needs deeper understanding to derive latent structures
  - so: study ChatGPT on topic segmentation + discourse parsing -> deep semantic understanding (linear + hierarchical)
- Method
  - prompt with three components: task description, output format, structured input
  - task description = what to accomplish; output format = specified format, easy to extract linear/hierarchical structure; structured input = organized content to analyze
  - experiments run two times; four topic segmentation datasets, two discourse parsing datasets; average performance reported
- Findings
  - good understanding of linear topic structures in general domain; struggles in specific domain
  - can hardly understand hierarchical rhetorical structures
  - analysis: more reasonable topic structures than human annotations; parses rhetorical structures only linearly
- Further studies
  - ICL: does not help linear structures; improves hierarchical; chain-of-thought contributes most
  - ablation of prompt components: output format most important -> insights for crafting prompts
  - instruction following: not fully followed on all datasets -> robustness still a concern
- Closing: hope for solid foundation for future dialogue discourse analysis research

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
With the development of generative models, large language models such as ChatGPT have shown remarkable capability on many natural language generation (NLG) and natural language understanding (NLU) tasks. But there is still no qualitative and quantitative evaluation of ChatGPT on dialogue discourse analysis. We think such an evaluation is vital, because it can uncover the potential of ChatGPT for deep semantic understanding of conversations.

Dialogue discourse analysis is crucial in natural language processing (NLP) because it reveals the underlying topic, coherence and rhetorical structures in a dialogue. Most previous work focuses on two things, dialogue topic segmentation and discourse parsing, which study the linear topic structures and the hierarchical rhetorical structures, as shown in Figure 1. ChatGPT is the most recent language generation capability, and how well it understands discourse structure is still largely uncharted. Some NLP tasks only need a shallow semantic understanding to extract the output from the input, but dialogue discourse analysis is a unique challenge for LLMs, because it needs a deeper semantic understanding to derive the latent discourse structures. So our study looks at how ChatGPT performs on topic segmentation and discourse parsing, to explore its capability in deep semantic understanding, both linear topic structure and hierarchical rhetorical structure.

To do this, we first made a prompt with three components: task description, output format and structured input. The task description tells ChatGPT what it needs to do, the output format tells ChatGPT to output in a specified format so we can easily extract the linear/hierarchical structure for evaluation, and the structured input gives ChatGPT organized content to analyze. Then we ran the experiments two times on four popular topic segmentation datasets and two discourse parsing datasets and reported the average performance.

- Findings: good on linear topic structures in general domain, struggles in specific domain; hardly understands hierarchical rhetorical structures; gives more reasonable topic structures than human annotations but parses rhetorical structures only linearly
- ICL: does not help linear structures, improves hierarchical; chain-of-thought contributes most
- Ablation: output format plays most important role -> insights for crafting prompts
- Instruction following: not fully followed on all datasets -> robustness an issue
- Closing: hope for solid foundation for future research

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
With the development of generative models, large language models such as ChatGPT have shown remarkable capability on many natural language generation (NLG) and natural language understanding (NLU) tasks. But there is still no qualitative and quantitative evaluation of ChatGPT on dialogue discourse analysis. We think such an evaluation is vital, because it can uncover the potential of ChatGPT for deep semantic understanding of conversations.

Dialogue discourse analysis is crucial in natural language processing (NLP) because it reveals the underlying topic, coherence and rhetorical structures in a dialogue. Most previous work focuses on two things, dialogue topic segmentation and discourse parsing, which study the linear topic structures and the hierarchical rhetorical structures, as shown in Figure 1. ChatGPT is the most recent language generation capability, and how well it understands discourse structure is still largely uncharted. Some NLP tasks only need a shallow semantic understanding to extract the output from the input, but dialogue discourse analysis is a unique challenge for LLMs, because it needs a deeper semantic understanding to derive the latent discourse structures. So our study looks at how ChatGPT performs on topic segmentation and discourse parsing, to explore its capability in deep semantic understanding, both linear topic structure and hierarchical rhetorical structure.

To do this, we first made a prompt with three components: task description, output format and structured input. The task description tells ChatGPT what it needs to do, the output format tells ChatGPT to output in a specified format so we can easily extract the linear/hierarchical structure for evaluation, and the structured input gives ChatGPT organized content to analyze. Then we ran the experiments two times on four popular topic segmentation datasets and two discourse parsing datasets and reported the average performance.

The experimental results show that ChatGPT understands linear topic structures well in the general domain, but it struggles with the topic structure of a specific domain. Also, ChatGPT can hardly understand the hierarchical rhetorical structures. When we analyze it more, ChatGPT can give topic structures that are more reasonable than the human annotations, but it only parses the hierarchical rhetorical structures linearly.

We also tried to enhance ChatGPT's abilities for deep semantic understanding by using In Context Learning (ICL). The results show that ICL does not help ChatGPT understand linear structures, but it does improve its ability to understand hierarchical structures. The chain-of-thought method of ICL contributes the most here.

We also did ablation experiments on the different prompt components. The ablation shows that the output format is the most important one. This gives some insights for crafting prompts when studying dialogue discourse analysis.

Last, we looked at whether ChatGPT follows the instructions, and found that ChatGPT does not fully follow the instructions on all the datasets. This means the robustness of ChatGPT is still a concern.

We hope our study can give a solid foundation for future research on dialogue discourse analysis.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
With the development of generative models, large language models (e.g., ChatGPT) have exhibited remarkable capability on various natural language generation (NLG) [1,2,3,4] and understanding (NLU) [5,6,7,8] tasks. However, there is still no qualitative and quantitative evaluation of ChatGPT on dialogue discourse analysis. Such an evaluation is vital to uncover the potential of ChatGPT for deep semantic understanding of conversations.

Dialogue discourse analysis plays a crucial role in natural language processing (NLP) by revealing the underlying topic, coherence, and rhetorical structures in a dialogue. Most previous work in this field focuses on dialogue topic segmentation [10,11,12,13,14] and discourse parsing [15,16,17,18,19], which study the linear topic structures and hierarchical rhetorical structures, respectively, as shown in Figure 1. Considering ChatGPT as the most recent language generation capability, the potential of its discourse structure understanding remains largely uncharted. Unlike some NLP tasks that only require a shallow semantic understanding to extract the output from the input, dialogue discourse analysis poses a unique challenge for LLMs, since it requires a deeper semantic understanding to derive the latent discourse structures. Therefore, our study examines the performance of ChatGPT on topic segmentation and discourse parsing to explore its capability in deep semantic understanding, including linear topic structure and hierarchical rhetorical structure.

To this end, we first crafted a prompt consisting of three components: task description, output format, and structured input. The task description tells ChatGPT what needs to be accomplished, the output format instructs ChatGPT to output in a specified format from which the linear/hierarchical structure can easily be extracted for evaluation, and the structured input provides ChatGPT with the organized content to be analyzed. Then, we ran the experiments two times on four popular topic segmentation datasets and two discourse parsing datasets and reported the average performance.

Experimental results show that ChatGPT has a good understanding of linear topic structures in the general domain but struggles to understand the topic structure of a specific domain. Besides, ChatGPT can hardly understand the hierarchical rhetorical structures. In-depth analysis reveals that ChatGPT can give more reasonable topic structures than human annotations but only parses the hierarchical rhetorical structures linearly.

In addition, to enhance the abilities of ChatGPT for deep semantic understanding, we explored the effect of In Context Learning (ICL). The results show that ICL could not help ChatGPT understand linear structures but improves its ability to understand hierarchical structures. Notably, the chain-of-thought method of ICL contributes the most.

Furthermore, we conducted ablation experiments to explore the role of the various prompt components. The ablation results reveal that the output format plays the most important role, which provides some insights into crafting prompts for studying dialogue discourse analysis.

Finally, we studied the instruction-following abilities of ChatGPT and found that ChatGPT can not fully follow the instructions on all datasets, indicating that the robustness of ChatGPT is still an issue of concern.

We hope that our study can provide a solid foundation for future research on dialogue discourse analysis.
